metadata.case_name: TING SIU KI v. WUN CHE MING AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: fireman for the Fire Services Department

injuries.description: Trigger finger over the right middle finger PIPJ
source: trigger finger condition over the right middle finger PIPJ
The provisional diagnosis made by the attending doctor at the A&E was “right middle finger injury” and “right middle finger PIPJ trigger finger”.
An operation for the release of the right middle finger triggering was performed on 31 July 2009 at POH.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of flexor muscle, fascia or tendon of other finger at wrist or hand level

injuries.description: Mild soft tissue sprain of right wrist and mild soft tissue compression injury of right middle finger PIPJ
injuries.body_part: right wrist and right middle finger PIPJ
source: Judging from the above evidence, Mr Ting probably sustained mild soft tissue sprain of his right wrist and mild soft tissue compression injury of right middle finger PIPJ as a result of the accident if it did occur the way he described.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified multiple injuries of wrist or hand

manifestations.description: He immediately felt pain in his right forearm and right palm.
he already felt numbness in his right hand
his middle finger was folded up and could not be straightened.
Trigger finger over right middle finger PIPJ was recorded.
tenderness over the right middle finger PIPJ.
there was swelling on his right hand finger.
He demonstrates reduced right middle finger active movement but passive movement is full.
1.5 cm surgical scar over base of his right middle finger, well-healed.
He also complains of reduced sensation over volar side of his middle finger.
During the grip-strength testing he demonstrates very much weakened right hand grip strength, only about 1/5 that of his left hand

treatments_received.treatment: Release of the right middle finger triggering (surgical)
source: An operation for the release of the right middle finger triggering was performed on 31 July 2009 at POH.
The plaintiff was followed up at the outpatient clinic at POH and physiotherapy and occupational therapy treatments were given there.
The plaintiff was followed up at the outpatient clinic at POH and physiotherapy and occupational therapy treatments were given there.
The plaintiff was given analgesic for pain relief.

treatments_received.treatment: A&E examination, treatment and referral to outpatient orthopaedic clinic at Pok Oi Hospital
source: When the plaintiff was first admitted to the Accident and Emergency Department (“A&E”) of Tuen Mun Hospital (“TMH”) at around 5:09 pm on 15 May 2009, it has been recorded by the doctor who attended him on the A&E record sheet (“the A&E record sheet") that the plaintiff had sustained right hand injury when “pulling on car door today when there is a car collided from back”.

The doctor at the A&E finished examining and treating the plaintiff at around 6:50 pm on the same day. He was discharged and was referred to the outpatient orthopaedic clinic at Pok Oi Hospital (“POH”) for follow-up treatment.

losses.description: Residual pain over the middle finger scar and reduced function of right middle finger following trigger finger and surgery.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: He avoids using his right hand for heavy duty at work, and taking precaution when playing sports.

comparable_cases.case_name: Singh Harpel v Najib Transport (2009) DCPI 494 of 2009 (HH Judge Lok; 23 Nov 2009)
comparable_cases.injury_description: swelling to his right hand with no fracture or dislocation. For the swelling and impending compartment syndrome, an emergency operation of fasciotomy was performed. Some residual stiffness and numbness of the hand was claimed.
